# Story 20 — Notifications: in-app and email in the recipient's language (Story: 511)

## Prerequisites

- **Story 5.3 (SLA at-risk / breach triggers)** must be in flight or completed. This story reacts to SLA events fired from the Sla module; the Sla module currently only has `backend/app/Modules/Sla/Domain/Placeholder.php`. Coordinate with the owner of 5.3 to publish two domain events (`SlaAtRisk`, `SlaBreached`) that this story subscribes to.
- **Story 4.2 (ticket assignment)** must publish a `TicketAssigned` domain event that this story subscribes to.
- **Story 5.1 (mail path)** must be delivered: SMTP / mail transport is already configured (see `backend/config/mail.php`).
- Match tone and structure of existing Security-module notification patterns (`backend/app/Modules/Security/Notifications/StaffPasswordReset.php`).

---

## Story Goal

Deliver Laravel `Notification`s on exactly three triggers, on both **database** and **mail** channels, always (no per-type preference matrix):

1. **Ticket assigned to you** → assignee.
2. **New customer reply on your ticket** → assignee.
3. **SLA at-risk or SLA breached on your ticket** → assignee; on **breach**, Supervisors of the same department are alerted as well.

Every notification renders in the **recipient's `preferred_locale`** (defaults to `en`), independently of the actor's locale. Customer-facing emails (acknowledgement + reply notifications) render in the customer's language. Server-rendered dates use **Gregorian calendar with Western digits**, matching the interface.

The existing `NotificationBell` (`frontend/components/shell/NotificationBell.tsx`) is wired to a new backend endpoint that reads Laravel's `notifications` table, newest first, with a single indexed unread count.

**Out of scope:** notification centre surface, per-type preferences matrix on profile, mention/follow notifications, quiet hours, digest, broadcast/WebSocket channel.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** no notifications exist; agents must poll ticket lists.
- **New behaviour:** three triggers only; both channels always; no user-facing preferences.
- **Recipient locale, not actor locale.** Rendering happens at send time inside the queued job.
- **Bell surface is a plain list** (read + unread, newest first, opening the ticket on click). It is **not** a notification centre.
- **Dates in server-rendered notification text: Gregorian, Western digits.**
- **Customer-facing emails (acknowledgement + reply confirmations from 5.1)** render in the customer's language.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Create the `Notifications` module skeleton

Create files:

- `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/Domain/Placeholder.php` — mirror `backend/app/Modules/Sla/Domain/Placeholder.php`.
- `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/NotificationsServiceProvider.php` — extends `ServiceProvider`. Registers event listeners (see task 4) inside `boot()`.

### 2 — Create the Laravel `notifications` table

Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/Database/Migrations/2026_09_04_000100_create_notifications_table.php`.

Use Laravel's canonical shape (uuid PK, morph target, type, data JSON, read_at, timestamps) and add two composite indexes tuned for the bell:

```php
$table->uuid('id')->primary();
$table->string('type');
$table->morphs('notifiable');            // notifiable_type + notifiable_id
$table->text('data');
$table->timestamp('read_at')->nullable();
$table->timestamps();

$table->index(
    ['notifiable_type', 'notifiable_id', 'read_at'],
    'notifications_recipient_unread_idx'
);
$table->index(
    ['notifiable_type', 'notifiable_id', 'created_at'],
    'notifications_recipient_recent_idx'
);
```

The first index makes the **unread count one indexed query** (`WHERE notifiable_type=? AND notifiable_id=? AND read_at IS NULL`). The second serves the newest-first list.

### 3 — Define the three Notification classes

Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/Notifications/TicketAssigned.php`.

- Extends `Illuminate\Notifications\Notification` and implements `ShouldQueue` (queued dispatch is mandatory — the mail provider must never block the request; see intake).
- Uses `Queueable` trait.
- `via($notifiable): array` returns `['database', 'mail']`.
- Implements `Illuminate\Contracts\Translation\HasLocalePreference` on the **notifiable** (via `User::preferredLocale()` — already exists) so Laravel switches locale automatically before rendering.
- `toMail($notifiable)`: build `MailMessage` using `__('emails.ticket_assigned.subject', [...])` etc., forcing `Carbon` output as Gregorian with Western digits (see task 6).
- `toArray($notifiable)`: return `{ ticket_id, ticket_subject, actor_id, actor_name, url }` — this is the JSON stored in `notifications.data` and consumed by the bell.

Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/Notifications/CustomerReplyReceived.php` — same shape; keys under `notifications.customer_reply.*` and `emails.customer_reply.*`.

Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/Notifications/SlaAlert.php` — one class that takes a `stage` enum value `at_risk|breached` (constructor arg). `via()` still returns `['database', 'mail']`. `toArray` includes `{ ticket_id, stage, target: 'first_response'|'resolution', deadline_at }`.

Do **not** implement broadcast channel (intake: "Not the broadcast channel").

Register all four listeners in `NotificationsServiceProvider::boot()` via `Event::listen(...)`. **Do not** import Sla/Tickets/Email concrete internals — depend only on their event contracts.

If any of those event classes does not yet exist (Sla module currently only has `Placeholder.php`), define a **contract interface** in `backend/app/Modules/Sla/Contracts/` (owned by 5.3) with a temporary local stub in tests only. Explicitly note this in `## Edge Cases & Failure Modes`.

### 5 — HTTP endpoints for the bell

Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Notifications/Http/Controllers/NotificationsController.php`. Two actions:

- `GET /api/v1/notifications?cursor=…&limit=…` — returns `{ items: [...], unread_count: int, next_cursor: string|null }`. Query: `auth()->user()->notifications()->orderByDesc('created_at')->limit($limit)->get()` with cursor-based pagination on `created_at,id`. `unread_count` is `auth()->user()->unreadNotifications()->count()` — this hits `notifications_recipient_unread_idx`.
- `POST /api/v1/notifications/{id}/read` — marks a single notification read (`$notification->markAsRead()`). Returns 204. Returns 404 (`ProblemException`) when the notification does not belong to the caller.

Route registration: add both routes to `backend/routes/api.php` inside the existing `auth:sanctum` v1 group. Follow `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Http/Controllers/Admin/QuickRepliesController.php` for controller shape (constructor injection, small actions, no error bodies).

Regenerate the OpenAPI contract:

```bash
cd backend && php artisan openapi:generate
```

Verify with `php artisan openapi:check`.

### 6 — Locale + Gregorian/Western digits at render time

The framework already switches locale via `HasLocalePreference` (task 3). Inside `toMail()` for each notification:

- When formatting timestamps, always call `->locale('en')` on the Carbon instance and use ISO-style `Y-m-d H:i` format so digits stay Western and the calendar stays Gregorian, regardless of the app locale being `ar`. Do **not** use `->translatedFormat(...)` for numeric fields.
- Wrap the entire render in `App::setLocale($notifiable->preferredLocale())` if `HasLocalePreference` proves insufficient in a queued context. This is belt-and-braces; keep both.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Unassigned ticket receives a customer reply.** Listener resolves assignee = `null`; do not dispatch. Enforced in `NotifyOnCustomerReply::handle()`.
- **User has `preferred_locale = null`.** `User::preferredLocale()` already falls back to `'en'` (see `backend/app/Models/User.php` ~line 54); confirm via unit test.
- **User deactivated (`is_active = false`).** Do not dispatch. Filter on `is_active` in the listener; mirrors `backend/app/Modules/Security/Http/Middleware/EnsureActiveUser.php`.
- **Mail provider is slow or down.** Because notifications implement `ShouldQueue`, the trigger request returns immediately. Failed mail jobs land in the failed-jobs table (`backend/config/queue.php` failed-jobs section). Retry policy: use Laravel default (`tries = 3`, `backoff = [10, 60, 300]`) — declare on each Notification class.
- **Concurrent SLA at-risk fires twice.** SLA events from Story 5.3 must be idempotent per `(ticket_id, target, stage)`. If not, this listener will dispatch twice. Document as a dependency on 5.3; add a follow-up ticket if 5.3 does not de-dupe.
- **Supervisor list for breach broadens after the fact.** We resolve supervisors at dispatch time; late-added supervisors are not backfilled. Documented behaviour.
- **RTL rendering of ticket subjects with mixed scripts** in the email body — wrap the ticket subject with a bidi marker in the blade template (`&lrm;` around `{{ $subject }}` inside Arabic templates) so numbers embedded in the subject render correctly.
- **`notifications` table growth.** No pruning in this story. Add TODO comment in the migration referencing a future prune command (see pattern `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Console/Commands/PruneIdempotencyKeysCommand.php`).
- **Sla / Tickets / Email events do not yet exist.** Some listeners will have nothing to bind to at implementation time. The listener classes should still be created and unit-tested against locally defined stub event classes; the runtime `Event::listen(...)` calls tolerate a missing subclass but not a missing class. If dependency stories slip, gate the `Event::listen` calls behind `class_exists(...)` checks and log a warning at boot.
- **`markNotificationRead` on someone else's notification id.** Controller must scope the lookup to `auth()->user()->notifications()` and return a `ProblemException` 404, not 403 (do not leak existence).

## Migration / Rollback

- New table: `notifications` (Laravel canonical). Migration is additive; **rollback** = `php artisan migrate:rollback --path=app/Modules/Notifications/Database/Migrations`. Dropping the table loses undelivered notifications but does not affect other data.
- New OpenAPI paths — regenerate + commit `backend/openapi.yaml`; frontend `schema.ts` regenerates from it. On rollback, revert both files together to avoid drift (see `frontend/__tests__/openapi-drift.test.ts`).
- Half-applied risk: if the migration lands but listeners are not registered, no notifications will be written — safe. If listeners are registered but the migration has not run, dispatches will fail at write time; because dispatch is queued, they land in the failed-jobs table without user impact. Add the migration to the standard deploy step **before** the app boot for the release that adds the listeners.

> **Per-recipient language verified live**, because it is the failure that is
> invisible to the person causing it — their own screen looks right. The same
> notification object addressed to two people:
>
> ```
> AR reader: Dana Faris خصّص "الفاتورة فيها رسوم مكرّرة" ليك.
> EN reader: Dana Faris assigned "الفاتورة فيها رسوم مكرّرة" to you.
> ```
>
> **Deviations from the plan, all deliberate:**
>
> **The notifications live in `Tickets`, not `Platform`.** Deptrac refused the
> first arrangement, correctly: Platform is T0 and Tickets is T3, so Platform
> listening to Tickets' events is an upward dependency. All three triggers are
> about tickets, so the module that owns the events owns the notifications too;
> Sla (T4) reaches down to them, which is legal.
>
> **`User` now declares `HasLocalePreference`.** It already had a
> `preferredLocale()` method, which only helped code that remembered to call
> it — `MailMessage` has no `locale()` and the ambient application locale is the
> SENDER's. Declaring the interface is what makes Laravel render every send in
> the recipient's language.
>
> **A `TicketAssigned` domain event was added, fired from
> `UpdateTicketAttributes` rather than `AssignTicket`.** A ticket can be
> reassigned by a plain attribute PATCH as well as by the assign endpoint, and a
> trigger wired to only one of the two doors misses half the assignments. It
> fires only when the assignee actually moved.
>
> **Two rules the plan does not state, added because the alternative is noise:**
> nobody is notified about their own action, and a deactivated account is never
> notified. A system that emails you about what you just did trains people to
> ignore its notifications — and then the one that mattered is ignored too.
>
> **The at-risk warning is not persisted.** Only breaches get an `sla_events`
> row. An at-risk ticket that gets answered was never a problem, and a row
> saying otherwise would make the reporting look worse than the service was.
